title: The world born of hunger
hookLine: a second creation story: at first there was nothing, covered by death, which is hunger, and hunger made the world
carry: the world is food and eater; offer first
tomorrow: the gods and demons and the breath
last: ASHVAMEDHA — THE WHOLE WORLD IS THE OFFERING.

lines: TWENTY DAYS AGO: BEING ALONE, CALM.
TWO STORIES, KEPT SIDE BY SIDE.
cards: In the beginning there was nothing here at all. All this was covered by death. And death, it says, is hunger.
That's the first sentence of the Brihadaranyaka's second section. Twenty days ago, Uddalaka told his son a calmer story: in the beginning there was Being alone, and it thought, let me be many.
Two great Upanishads, two creation stories. Hindu tradition has kept them both, side by side.

teach.b: In Sanskrit: naiveha kimcanagra asit, mrityunaivedam avritam asit, ashanayaya. Ashanaya hi mrityuh: for hunger is death. Then death does something.
It makes a mind, thinking: let me have a self. It moves about, chanting praise, and from its praise water arises. The froth on the water hardens into the earth.
Death toils, and from its heat, fire is born. Through the mind it joins with speech, and the year is born.

teach.h: THE NEWBORN YEAR CRIES OUT: BHAN!
teach.b: Death opens its mouth to swallow the newborn year, and the year cries out, bhan! That cry becomes speech. Death thinks: if I eat this, I'll have less food.
So instead, through speech, it brings forth everything: the verses of the Vedas, the rituals, people, animals. And whatever it brings forth, it begins to eat.
Then death's body swells, and the text plays on a word: the swollen one, ashva, the horse. Yesterday's horse, back again.

teach.h: ALL THIS IS FOOD AND EATER.
teach.b: A few pages later the same Upanishad sums it up: this whole world is just food and the eater of food. That's the teaching to keep.
Many teachers read it this way: eating is never only eating; it's part of the great sacrifice the world is made of.

Many teachers connect this to what Hindu families do every day: before eating, they offer the food first, at the home shrine or with a short prayer, and what comes back is prasad, a gift. Hunger runs all the way down.
Offering first is how a Hindu turns that hunger into worship.

how: Many Hindu families offer food at the home shrine or with a short prayer before eating, and receive it back as prasad; teachers often connect this to the Vedic picture of the world as food and the eater of food.

o: hunger, which the text calls death
the fire that eats every offering

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.

s: in Hindu homes, food is often offered first and then eaten as prasad
offering first turns the meal from just eating into worship.
the text says hunger is death
in this story, the world begins calm and full
it begins with nothing, covered by death, which is hunger. the calm story of Being alone is the Chandogya's.

games.q: you're death, in this story. you've just brought forth the year, and you open your mouth to eat it. it cries out. what do you do?
o: think: if I eat this, I'll have less food, and bring forth everything else instead.
give up and go back to nothing.
games.why: death spares it, and through speech brings forth the Vedas, rituals, people and animals, and then begins to eat all it made.

practice: Notice any hunger in you right now: for food, for your phone, for something to happen. Don't act on it; watch it rise. Then picture your next meal in front of you.
If you pray, offer it silently first, the way many Hindu families do, to God, to Krishna, to whoever you call on, and only then imagine taking the first bite.
If you don't pray, simply pause before it and give thanks for everyone and everything that became this food.

wordCard.voice: Ashanaya, hunger. The Brihadaranyaka's creation: nothing, covered by death, which is hunger, and from that hunger, mind, water, earth, fire, speech and a world of food and eaters.

orig.note: Sanskrit aśanāyā: hunger, the wish to eat. aśanāyā hi mṛtyuḥ: for hunger is death.

carryVoice: Your line: the world is food and eater; offer first. Tomorrow, the gods go looking for a singer. That's day three hundred sixty-one.
